medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: A Leave of Absence (LOA) for a period of time as long as 12 months or one academic year may be granted by the Dean to a student for treatment of a medical condition, maternity or paternity reasons, or other exceptional circumstances. Students must generally be in good academic standing (that is, having a grade point average of 2.0 or higher and not being on probation for any reason) to be granted a LOA. Exceptions may be made on a case-by-case basis. Academic difficulties, in and of themselves, will not be considered a valid reason for requesting a LOA. Generally, a LOA is discouraged for any student prior to the completion of one year of medical school. The student will usually be expected to repeat any course work deemed incomplete by course coordinators at the time the LOA begins. The exact length of the Leave of Absence may vary from case to case; however, it shall not normally exceed one year. Students may initiate a LOA by writing to the Dean(s) for Student Affairs. medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Students not only receive a great medical education, but they also have the opportunity to participate in "the  other education" through involvement in more than 15 active student interest groups. These groups range from medical specialty interest groups to religious and community service organizations. The wide variety of groups available allows every student to get involved in the local community by working with fellow students with similar interests. For more information about student involvement, visit our website at:  https://medicine.tamu.edu/academics/students/organizations/index.html .
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The School of Medicine offers exceptional training on four campuses in Bryan-College Station, Dallas, Houston, and Round Rock.  The school is headquartered at the Health Professions Education Building on the Texas A&M Health Science Center Bryan Campus. Each campus has a distinct environment and various offerings for education and lifestyle. The Bryan campus is located just west of Texas A&M University in College Station, Texas, 100 miles northwest of Houston. Bryan-College Station, affectionately referred to as Aggieland, is home to approximately 203,000 people and is located in East-Central Texas between the Brazos and Navasota Rivers.  For more information on our campus communities go to our website at https://medicine.tamu.edu/campuses/index.html
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Although on-campus housing is not available, apartment living complexes surround our campuses, some walking distance or a bike-ride away from our facilities. Our Student Affairs Program Coordinators at all of our campus communities provide access to apartment listings and roommate search options. Rents for unfurnished apartments range from $400 to $1,200 per month.

medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
Pre-Clerkship
The first 18 months of the curriculum focus on the fundamentals of biomedical science and consist of two components as follows:  Students start the first year of medical school with the foundations blocks, which continue through mid-April of the first calendar year. Foundations blocks emphasize the basic structure of the human body and basic principles of other medical science disciplines: gross anatomy, histology, basic principles of biochemistry, genetics, pharmacology and cell physiology. This also includes Neuroscience and Introduction to Disease, which covers basic pathophysiology, immunology and bacteriology. In addition to the basic medical sciences, students take integrated courses in the practice of medicine block, which cover medical humanities, ethics, leadership and other important professional development topics, as well as introduction to clinical skills, which includes patient history-taking and doctor-patient communication skills and physical diagnosis.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms:
The Primary Care & Population Health Department is committed to full-scope family medicine and community care. Through our keen focus on rural populations and innovative care delivery, we’re eliminating health disparities in Texas and bringing health care where it’s needed most. We utilize our own clinical sites and a select group of clinical affiliates to provide excellent educational settings for faculty, students and residents for a community-based approach to preventive healthcare. Our faculty consists of academic clinicians practicing behavioral health, family medicine, geriatrics, gynecology, internal medicine, obstetrics, palliative care, and sports medicine. URL: https://medicine.tamu.edu/departments/index.html

The Texas A&M HSC Rural & Community Health Institute (ARCHI) is a health extension center to improve access to healthcare and reduce disparities in health status and outcomes by improving the quality and safety of healthcare. 
URL: https://architexas.org/about/.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Key areas of collaborative research include alcoholism, cardiovascular diseases, cancer biology, molecular pathogenesis of infectious agents, experimental therapeutics and drug development, primary protein structure and function, and aging and developmental biology. There are two dual degree programs, the M.D./Ph.D. and the M.D. Plus programs that offer formal and extensive research training leading to the PhD or MS degree in conjunction with the M.D. degree. For students interested in a less extensive research experience we offer the Medical Scholar Research Pathway Program. In addition to our in-house programs, there are many external summer and "year-off" research training programs that allow a medical student to either stay at the Texas A&M University School of Medicine or move to a different location for a defined training period.  For more information, see https://medicine.tamu.edu/omsre/index.html
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: The Pre-Clerkship portion is an 18-month long competency-based curriculum organized in blocks and focusing on an enhanced level of integration between basic science knowledge and clinical application.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Service has always been a  priority for students at the School of Medicine. Each class chooses to support human service organizations throughout the course of their medical education experience.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
As one of the most comprehensive medical colleges in the nation, students have the flexibility to select areas of specialization to customize a program to fit their individual needs and aspirations. Texas A&M University Texas A&M Naresh K. Vashisht College of Medicine offers the following dual degrees:
•  Doctor of Medicine (MD)
•  Medical Science (MS and PhD)
•  MD/PhD
•  Integrated Engineering and Medicine (EnMed) dual degrees (M.E./MD)
The Following master's degrees are for admitted MD students:
•  MD+ Master of Business Admin. (MBA)
•  MD+ Master of Public Health (MPH)
•  MD+Master of Science in Medical Sciences (MS)
•  MD+Master of Science in Education for Healthcare Professionals (MS)
•  MD+Master of Science in Science and Technology Journalism (MS)
•  MD+Master of Jurisprudence, Health Law, Policy, & Management
•  MD+Master of Entrepreneurial Leadership & Innovation
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
Our MISSION is to improve the health and well-being of the people of Texas through excellence in education, research and health care delivery.  Founded by the Teague-Cranston Act, the Texas A&M University Naresh K. Vashisht College of Medicine was created to serve the under-served populations of Texas with the core values of Texas A&M University, namely Respect, Excellence, Leadership, Loyalty, Integrity and Selfless Service. 

Our VISION is to develop the innovators and leaders in medicine and biomedical research who will transform American medicine in the 21st century.
THREE DISTINCT PRIORITIES.  Established in 1977 with a charter class of 32 students, the College of Medicine has evolved into a dynamic, student-centered institution focused on the future of medicine and advancing three distinct priorities:  
(1) Transformational Education for All Students: Bolstering each student’s education by giving life-changing experiences and granting timely graduation with low debt 
(2) Discovery and Innovation for the World: Addressing the world’s most formidable problems through collaborative research and entrepreneurial approaches 
(3) Influence on the State, Nation and the World: Integrating Texas A&M’s land-grant origins with its top-tier research strengths to serve the state, nation and world
THREE AREAS OF FOCUS distinguish the College of Medicine:
(1) Rural Population Health: The Naresh K. Vashisht College of Medicine brings health care where it’s needed most. Through our keen focus on rural populations and innovative care delivery, the college eliminates health disparities throughout Texas.
(2) Military and Aerospace Medicine: The College of Medicine honors Texas A&M University’s rich military legacy. Through our unique relationship with the TAMU Corps of Cadets, military academies and veteran populations, the college improves the lives of military members and their families.
(3) Innovation Through Engineering: The College of Medicine makes the impossible, possible - by creating systems and technologies that address health care’s greatest challenges and bringing together the brightest minds in health care and engineering.
MEDICAL EDUCATION is the thread that creates a singular vision for future and current students, researchers, alumni and practicing physicians. By impacting education and training at all levels, the College of Medicine fosters achievement of career goals and the transformation of health care for patient populations. Our curriculum brings flexibility and individualization to the education process, to create lifelong-learners and bring better health care to all. The College of Medicine implements an updated and fully integrated curriculum providing students with a pre-clerkship curriculum of 18 months. Students embark on their pre-clerkship training at the Bryan-College Station campus for 12 months and then transition to their campus designations for the remaining 3 years of training. Students have several options for study across our campuses – each has a distinct environment and offerings for education and lifestyle. The school provides clinical training through affiliated medical facilities in Bryan-College Station, Corpus Christi, Dallas, Fort Hood, Houston, Round Rock San Antonio. The school is committed to providing an environment that promotes the Aggie Core Values, inclusiveness and compassion in its future physicians and scientists. Our emphasis on highly integrated materials, organ systems-based instruction and institutionalized programs for support between class years is proving to produce physicians with the knowledge, expertise and vision to meet the challenges facing today's.

ACCREDITATION.  In June 2020, the Texas A&M Naresh K. Vashisht College of Medicine was re-accredited by the Liaison Committee on Medical Education (LCME) for eight years, with the next site visit scheduled for the 2027–28 academic year.

medSchoolApplication.cbcRequired: Applicants accepted must submit to and satisfactorily complete a background check as a condition of matriculation. Admission will be final with the completion of the CBC and results deemed favorable.
medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: 5-10 business days, depending on time of year.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText:
If an applicant is no longer in undergraduate school and cannot obtain an evaluation from their health professions adviser or health professions advisory committee, they should proceed as follows:
• If attending graduate school, one evaluation must be from the applicant's graduate advisor, a major professor, or the chair of their major department.
• If an applicant has been out of college for more than one year and employed or serving in the military, one letter must be from the immediate supervisor or commanding officer.
• If self-employed, one of the letters must be from a business associate. The evaluation must detail the applicant's performance and extent of responsibilities.
• If an applicant cannot obtain a letter from a health professions advisor or faculty member because they have been out of school for several years, they must submit at least two letters from employment supervisors, medical personnel, and/or research supervisors/mentors to complete the evaluation packet.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: A minimum of three letters of evaluation or a Health Professions Advisory Committee packet are required. Letters of reference from professors are preferred, and at least one letter must be from a research mentor. Letters from physicians, other medical personnel or employment supervisors are acceptable.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay:
An Interview Orientation is conducted on Monday from 10am - 12:30pm. The Interview Orientation include presentations, and medical student panels. The MMI Interview sessions are conducted via KIRA Platform beginning in late July and concluding in late January. The MMI sessions are conducted on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday. Applicants selected to interview for the MD/PhD program are conducted over two days.  MD/PhD applicants interview virtually for the PhD program on Wednesdays. 

EnMed applicants interview are conducted in -person on Mondays on the Houston Methodist Hospital campus. 

Applicants will NOT be considered for interview until the primary and secondary applications and supplemental documents are completed AND submitted and the $60 application fee is received.
medSchoolApplication.interviewInvitations: Interview invitations sent approximately two-three weeks in advance of an interview session date. Interviews begin on July, 2026 and conclude approximately January, 2027.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: For the MD and EnMed programs, the format is the Multiple Mini Interview (MMI). Each applicant is given (six) 5-minute stations and one 15-minute personal interview assessing interpersonal skills and competencies across multiple categories.
medSchoolApplication.regionalInterview: For the Regular MD program, interviews are conducted virtually via Kira Platform. All Engineering Medicine (EnMed) interviews are conducted in person at the Houston Methodist Hospital campus.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: Interviews are conducted virtually via Kira Platform. Video interviews are not an option for EnMed.

medSchoolApplication.stateResAfterMatric: Non-resident students accepted to the SOM may be eligible for in-state tuition and fees if awarded a SOM competitive, renewable scholarship of at least $1,000.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: By state mandate, enrollment of individuals who are residents of states other than Texas may not exceed 10 percent of the current class size.
medSchoolApplication.acceptCanadianApplInformation: U.S. citizens or U.S. permanent residents who have successfully completed 90 credit hours or earned a baccalaureate at a fully-accredited Canadian college or university are considered for admission.
medSchoolApplication.dacaDetail: Requires current DACA status to apply and at the time of medical school enrollment. Official documentation is required.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
The Admissions Committee has considered the impact of COVID-19 on applicants’ information.
The committee will exercise flexibility in reviewing courses, healthcare activities, and community service activities taken between June 2020 and June 2022 and consider that some of these activities were necessarily virtual and/or diminished in amount.  This should not be construed as an allowance for insufficient quantities of activities.  Applicants are always expected to have sufficient health care experience to allow the Admissions Committee to evaluate their interest and commitment to a career in medicine and sufficient community service experience to allow evaluate their compassion, altruism, and emotional intelligence. Medical School Pre-Requisites must be completed in-person. However, online/virtual exceptions may be considered by contacting Mr. Fernando Vasquez, Assistant Dean of MD Admissions.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: We will consider the highest MCAT score provided.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: MCAT scores below the 50th percentile are not considered competitive.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: Overall GPA's and BCPM GPA's below are 3.25 are not considered competitive.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: We consider all course work at all levels.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Dual Credit or pre-transfer coursework taken at a local community college is accepted towards the medical school pre-requisites.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: We only accept notice of Significant updates or achievements. We do not consider Letters of Interest or Intent.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Federal and State loan funds are available to students with financial need. Institutional merit and need-based recruiting scholarships are awarded on a competitive basis prior to matriculation.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: Admission is granted to students without regard to their financial status. Satisfactory academic progress is a term generally used in determining eligibility for continuing financial aid to a student. Maintenance of acceptable grades and a maximum limit of six years to complete the M.D. program are only a few of the details considered in determining if a student is making satisfactory progress. Generally a student must maintain a minimum of qualitative progress as measured by the Student Promotions Committee.

medSchoolPrograms.info:
The Summer Undergraduate Research Program gives students interested in pursuing a career in biomedical research the opportunity to work in a lab and conduct a research project during the summer. Students in the 10-week program work closely with College of Medicine faculty on research projects in basic or clinical science disciplines. Application deadline: 2/1/2026.

The MS in Medical Sciences prepares future researchers to bridge the interface between patient care and bench research, interact effectively with the spectrum of healthcare providers and community members, and function efficiently within large research teams. The curriculum is designed to provide a strong foundation in biological sciences along with scholarly activities. A MS in Medical Sciences will serve to:
1. Enhance coursework and other training to prepare for success in medical or graduate schools and in occupations
2. Increase your earning potential, job placement and advancement
Application deadline: 6/15/2026

Engineering Medicine - Integrated MD/ME (Masters in Engineering) 
Contact: Amy Wrigh, PhD - amywright1016@tamu.edu
URL: https://enmed.tamu.edu
Application Deadline: Oct. 1, 2026, 5 PM CST
Apply via TMDSAS for Texas Residents or AMCAS for non-Texas residents 

The Engineering Medicine (EnMed) program, started in 2020, delivered by the School of Engineering Medicine, is a parallel curriculum or track within TAMU COM’s medical education program. In partnership with Houston Methodist Hospital to educate a new kind of physician who will create transformational technology for health care. EnMed is a revolutionary program blending engineering design, entrepreneurship, and translation with medical training to produce the “physicianeer.”  EnMed students fulfill all academic/professional requirements for the MD and ME degrees in Houston. Engineering or computer science majors are preferred.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
Math-Based Statistics taught in the Math or Statistics Department. Statistics taught in other departments may be considered. The Stats course must cover:
Descriptive statistics
• Central tendency
• Variability or dispersion
• Kurtosis and skewness
• Univariate analysis
• Bivariate analysis
• Correlation/covariance

Inferential statistics
• Statistics modeling theory and assumptions (parametric and non-parametric)
• Population/sampling methods
• Inference/Probability
• Confidence intervals
• Chi-square probability
• General linear models (t-test, ANOVA, ANCOVA, regression analysis, multivariate methods)

Biochemistry taught in the departments of Biology, Biochemistry, or Chemistry at a four-year college. The course must cover: 
• pH, Protein structure/function
• Nucleic acid synthesis
• Carbohydrate metabolism
• Lipid structures/metabolism
• Amino acid metabolism
• Enzyme kinetics
• Electron transport
• Oxidative phosphorylation
• One carbon metabolism
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: Prerequisite coursework, particularly the biological sciences and chemistry coursework, must have been taken within 10 years of desired matriculation and must be taken in-person.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
The admissions committee makes a concerted effort to understand the circumstances of applicants and give careful consideration to their history of academic and MCAT performance. It carefully scrutinizes the characteristics and circumstances that reflect a meaningful record of accomplishment, resilience and experiences. In keeping with holistic review practices, applicants are screened on academic performance, motivation, healthcare experiences, community service, ability to communicate and interact effectively, and other compelling factors, such as:
•	leadership
•	personal statements
•	letters of evaluation
•	areas of interest in medicine
•	hardship circumstances
•	socioeconomic background or circumstances
•	first generation to attend and graduate from college
•	parents' education and occupations
•	military service 
•	responsible for personal care of others
•	region in which applicant resides
•	resident of underserved area
•	experience of other cultures
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: We prefer applicants with meaningful and consistent experiences in healthcare such as shadowing physicians and other ancillary health professionals, volunteering or employment in a hospital or clinic setting, earning healthcare certifications (EMT, Scribe, etc.), medical missions locally and abroad, etc. We especially appreciate these kinds of activities sustained over time.
